1G:
**Α, α, ἄλφα** (which see), τό, indecl., 
**alpha**, the first letter of the Greek alphabet. As a numeral, ά = 1, α = 1000. As a prefix, it appears to have at least two and perhaps three distinct senses: 
1. ἀ- (before a vowel, ἀν-) **negative**, as in ἄ-γνωστος, ἄ-δικος. 
2. ἀ-, ἁ- **copulative**, indicating community and fellowship, as in ἁ-πλοῦς, ἀ-κολουθέω, ἀ-δελφός. 
3. An **intensive** force (LS, s. α), as in ἀ-τενίζω is sometimes assumed (but see Boisacq, see word).
(AS)

25:
**ἀγαπάω**, -ῶ, 
[in LXX chiefly for אהב ;] 
**to love**, to feel and exhibit esteem and goodwill to a person, to prize and delight in a thing. 
1. **Of human affection, to men**: τ. πλησίον, [[40-matthew.5.43|Mat.5:43;]] τ. ἐχθρούς, ib. 44; to Christ, [[43-john.8.42|Jhn.8:42;]] to God, [[40-matthew.22.37|Mat.22:37;]] with accusative of thing(s), [[42-luke.11.43|Luk.11:43]], [[43-john.12.43|Jhn.12:43]], [[49-ephesians.5.25|Eph.5:25]], [[55-2-timothy.4.8|II Tim 4:8]], 10, [[58-hebrews.1.9|Heb.1:9]], [[60-1-peter.2.17|1Pe.2:17, 3:10]], [[61-2-peter.2.15|2Pe.2:15]], [[62-1-john.2.15|1Jn.2:15]], [[66-revelation.12.11|Rev.12:11]].
2. **Of divine love**; 
(a) **God's love**: to men, [[45-romans.8.37|Rom.8:37;]] to Christ, [[43-john.3.35|Jhn.3:35;]] 
(b) **Christ's love**: to men, [[41-mark.10.21|Mrk.10:21;]] to God, [[43-john.14.31|Jhn.14:31;]] with cogn. accusative, [[43-john.17.26|Jhn.17:26]], [[49-ephesians.2.4|Eph.2:4]].
_SYN._: φιλέω. From its supposed etymology (Thayer, LS; but see also Boisacq) ἀ. is commonly understood properly to denote love based on esteem (diligo), as distinct from that expressed by φιλέω (amo), spontaneous natural affection, emotional and unreasoning. If this distinction holds, ἀ. is fitly used in NT of Christian love to God and man, the spiritual affection which follows the direction of the will, and which, therefore, unlike that feeling which is instinctive and unreasoned, can be commanded as a duty. (Cf. ἀγάπη, and _v_. Tr., _Syn_. §xii; Cremer, 9, 592; and esp. MM, _VGT_, see word) (AS)

**ἀγάπη**, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX for אַהֲבָה, which is also rendered by ἀγάπησις and φιλία ;] 
**love, goodwill, esteem**. Outside of bibl. and eccl. books, there is no clear instance (with Deiss., _LAE_, 18:4, 70:2, cf. the same writer in _Constr. Quar._, ii, 4; and with MM, _VGT_, see word, cf. Dr. Moulton in _Exp. Times_, xxvi, 3, 139). In NT, like ἀγαπάω, -ῶ, 
1. **Of men's love**: 
(a) to one another, [[43-john.13.35|Jhn.13:35;]] 
(b) to God, [[62-1-john.2.5|1Jn.2:5.]]
2. **Of divine love**; 
(a) **God's love**: to men, [[45-romans.5.8|Rom.5:8;]] to Christ, [[43-john.17.26|Jhn.17:26;]] 
(b) **Christ's love to men**: [[45-romans.8.35|Rom.8:35.]] 
3. In pl., **love feasts**: Ju 12 (_DB_, iii, 157).
_SYN._: φιλία. ἀ., signifying properly (see: ἀγαπάω) love which chooses its object, is taken over from LXX, where its connotation is more general, into NT, and there used exclusively to express that spiritual bond of love between God and man and between man and man, in Christ, which is characteristic of Christianity. It is thusdistinct from φιλία, **friendship** ([[59-james.4.4|Jas.4:4]] only), στοργή, **natural affection** (in NT only in compounds, see: ἄστοργος) and ἔρως, **sexual love**, which is not used in NT, its place being taken by ἐπιθυμία. (Cf. ἀγαπάω; and see Abbott, _Essays_, 70f.; _DB_, vol. i., 555; Cremer, 13, 593; MM, _VGT_, see word). (AS)

39G:
**ἅγιος**, -α, ον 
(τό ἅγός, **religious awe**; ἅζω, **to venerate**), [in LXX chiefly for קֹ֫דֶשׁ ;] 
primarily, **dedicated to the gods, sacred** (Hdt.; rare in Att., never in Hom., Hes. and Trag., who use ἁγνός), hence, **holy**, characteristic of God, separated to God, worthy of veneration. 
1. ** Its highest application is to God himself, in his purity, majesty, and glory**: [[42-luke.1.49|Luk.1:49]], [[43-john.17.11|Jhn.17:11]], [[66-revelation.4.8|Rev.4:8]]. Hence 
(a) of things and places which have a claim to reverence as sacred to God, e.g. the Temple: [[40-matthew.24.15|Mat.24:15]], [[58-hebrews.9.1|Heb.9:1]]; 
(b) **of persons employed by him, as angels**: [[52-1-thessalonians.3.13|1Th.3:13;]] prophets, [[42-luke.1.70|Luk.1:70;]] apostles, [[49-ephesians.3.5|Eph.3:5.]] 
2. **Applied to persons as separated to God's service**: 
(a) of Christ, [[41-mark.1.24|Mrk.1:24]], [[43-john.6.69|Jhn.6:69]], [[44-acts.4.30|Act.4:30]]; 
(b) of Christians, [[44-acts.9.13|Act.9:13]], [[45-romans.1.7|Rom.1:7]], [[58-hebrews.6.10|Heb.6:10]], [[66-revelation.5.8|Rev.5:8]]. 
3. **In the moral sense of sharing God's purity**: [[41-mark.6.20|Mrk.6:20]], [[43-john.17.11|Jhn.17:11]], [[44-acts.3.14|Act.3:14]], [[66-revelation.3.7|Rev.3:7]].
4. **Of pure, clean sacrifices and offerings**: [[46-1-corinthians.7.14|1Co.7:14]], [[49-ephesians.1.4|Eph.1:4]]. 
_SYN._: ἁγνός, **pure**, both in ceremonial and spiritual sense; ἱερός (sacer), **sacred**, that which is inviolable because of its (external) relation to God; ὅσιος (sanctus as opposite to nefas), that which is based on everlasting ordinances of right. (Cf. Tr., _Syn._, §lxxxviii; _DB_, ii, 399 f.; Cremer, 34, 594-601; MM, _VGT_, see word) (AS)

(b) **of persons, truthful**: [[40-matthew.22.16|Mat.22:16]], [[41-mark.12.14|Mrk.12:14]], [[43-john.3.33|Jhn.3:33 7:18 8:26]], [[45-romans.3.4|Rom.3:4]], [[47-2-corinthians.6.8|2Co.6:8]].

235:
**ἀλλά** (ἀλλ᾽ usually bef. α and υ, often bef. ε and η, rarely bef. ο and ω, never bef. ι; Tdf., _Pr._, 93 f.; WH, _App._, 146), 
_adversative particle_, 
**stronger than δέ**; prop. neuter pl. of ἄλλος, used adverbially, with changed accent; hence prop. **otherwise, on the other hand** (cf. [[45-romans.3.31|Rom.3:31]]); 
1. opposing a previous negation, **but**: οὐ (μὴ) . . . ἀ., [[40-matthew.5.15|Mat.5:15, 17]] [[41-mark.5.39|Mrk.5:39]], [[43-john.7.16|Jhn.7:16]], al.; rhetorically subordinating but not entirely negativing what precedes, οὐ . . . ἀ., **not so much . . . as**, [[41-mark.9.37|Mrk.9:37]], [[40-matthew.10.20|Mat.10:20]], [[43-john.12.44|Jhn.12:44]], al.; with ellipse of the negation, [[40-matthew.11.7|Mat.11:7-9]], [[44-acts.19.2|Act.19:2]], [[46-1-corinthians.3.6|1Co.3:6 6:11 7:7]], [[47-2-corinthians.7.1|2Co.7:1]], [[48-galatians.2.3|Gal.2:3]], al.; in opposition to a foregoing pos. sentence, ἀ. οὐ, [[40-matthew.24.6|Mat.24:6]], [[46-1-corinthians.10.23|1Co.10:23]]; οὐ μόνον . . . ἀ. καί, [[43-john.5.18|Jhn.5:18]], [[45-romans.1.32|Rom.1:32]], al.; elliptically, after a negation, ἀ. ἵνα, [[41-mark.14.49|Mrk.14:49]], [[43-john.1.8|Jhn.1:8 9:3]], al.; = εἰ μή (Bl., §77, 13; M, _Pr._, 241; but cf. WM, §iii, 10), [[40-matthew.20.23|Mat.20:23]], [[41-mark.4.22|Mrk.4:22]]. 
2. Without previous negation, to express opposition, interruption, transition, etc., **but**: [[43-john.16.20|Jhn.16:20 12:27]], [[48-galatians.2.14|Gal.2:14]]; before commands or requests, [[44-acts.10.20|Act.10:20 26:16]], [[40-matthew.9.18|Mat.9:18]], [[41-mark.9.22|Mrk.9:22]], al.; to introduce an accessory idea, [[47-2-corinthians.7.11|2Co.7:11;]] in the apodosis after a condition or concession with εἰ, ἐάν, εἴπερ, **yet, still, at least**, [[41-mark.14.29|Mrk.14:29]], [[46-1-corinthians.9.2|1Co.9:2]], [[47-2-corinthians.4.16|2Co.4:16]], [[51-colossians.2.5|Col.2:5]], al.; after μέν, [[44-acts.4.17|Act.4:17]], [[45-romans.14.20|Rom.14:20]], [[46-1-corinthians.14.17|1Co.14:17]]; giving emphasis to the following clause, ἀλλ᾽ ἔρχεται ὥρα, **yea**, etc., [[43-john.16.2|Jhn.16:2;]] so with neg., ἀλλ᾽ οὐδέ, **nay, nor yet**, [[42-luke.23.15|Luk.23:15.]] 
3. Joined with other particles (a practice which increases in late writers; Simcox, _LNT_, 166), ἀ. γε, **yet at least**, [[42-luke.24.21|Luk.24:21]], [[46-1-corinthians.9.2|1Co.9:2]]; ἄ ἤ., **save only, except**, [[42-luke.12.51|Luk.12:51]], [[47-2-corinthians.1.13|2Co.1:13]]; ἀ. μὲν οὖν, [[50-philippians.3.8|Php.3:8]] (on this usage, see MM, _VGT_, see word). 
(AS)

302:
**ἄν**, 
_conditional particle_, 
which cannot usually be separately translated in English, its force depending on the constructions which contain it (see further, LS, see word; WM, §xlii; M, _Pr._, 165 ff.; MM, _VGT_, see word). 
1. In apodosis, 
(i) with indic, imperfect or aor., expressing what would be or would have been if (εἰ with impf., aor. or plpf.) some condition were or had been fulfilled: [[42-luke.7.39|Luk.7:39 17:6]], [[43-john.5.46|Jhn.5:46]], [[48-galatians.1.10|Gal.1:10]], [[40-matthew.12.7|Mat.12:7 24:43]], [[46-1-corinthians.2.8|1Co.2:8]], [[44-acts.18.14|Act.18:14]], [[62-1-john.2.19|1Jn.2:19]], al. The protasis is sometimes understood (as also in cl.): [[40-matthew.25.27|Mat.25:27]], [[42-luke.19.23|Luk.19:23]]. In hypothetical sentences, expressing unreality, ἄν (as often in late writers, more rarely in cl.) is omitted: [[43-john.8.39|Jhn.8:39 15:24 19:11]], [[45-romans.7.7|Rom.7:7]], [[48-galatians.4.15|Gal.4:15]]; 
(ii) with opt., inf., ptcp. (cl.; see LS, see word; M, _Int._, §275; M, _Pr._, 167:4). 
2. In combination with conditional, relative, temporal, and final words; 
(i) as in cl., with subj., 
(a) in protasis with εἰ, in Attic contr. ἐάν, which see; 
(b) in conditional, relative, and temporal clauses (coalescing with ὅτε, ἐπεί, etc.; see: ὅταν, ἐπάν, etc.), **ever, soever**; 
(α) with pres., ἡνίκα, [[47-2-corinthians.3.15|2Co.3:15;]] ὃς ἄν, [[45-romans.9.15|Rom.9:15]] (LXX) 16:2, al.; ὅσοι ἄν, [[42-luke.9.5|Luk.9:5;]] ὡς ἄν, [[45-romans.15.24|Rom.15:24]] (M, _Pr._, 167); 
(β) with aor., ὃς ἄν, [[40-matthew.5.21|Mat.5:21, 22, 31]]; ἕως ἄν, **until**, [[40-matthew.2.13|Mat.2:13]], [[41-mark.6.10|Mrk.6:10]], al.; ὡς ἄν, **as soon as** (M, _Pr._, 167), [[46-1-corinthians.11.34|1Co.11:34]], [[50-philippians.2.23|Php.2:23]]. On the frequently use of ἐάν for ἄν with the foregoing words, see: ἐάν; 
(ii) in late Gk., when some actual fact is spoken of, with indic.: ὅταν (which see); ὅπου ἄν, [[41-mark.6.56|Mrk.6:56]] (M, _Pr._, 168); καθότι ἄν, [[44-acts.2.45|Act.2:45 4:35]]; ὡς ἄν, [[46-1-corinthians.12.2|1Co.12:2.]] 
3. in iterative construction, with imperfect and aor. indic. (M, _Pr._, 167): [[44-acts.2.45|Act.2:45 4:35]], [[46-1-corinthians.12.2|1Co.12:2]]. 
4. with optative, giving a potential sense to a question or wish: [[44-acts.8.31|Act.8:31 26:29]]. 
5. **Elliptical constructions**: εἰ μή τι ἄν (M, _Pr._, 169), [[46-1-corinthians.7.5|1Co.7:5;]] ὡς ἄν, with inf., **as it were** (op. cit. 167), [[47-2-corinthians.10.9|2Co.10:9.]]

**ἁρπαγμός**, οῦ, ὁ
(ἁρπάζω); 
1. prop., accusative, to the rule of its formation (Bl., § 27, 2), actively, the act of seizing, robbery (Plut., Deu Puer. Educ., p. 12A), [[50-philippians.2.6|Php.2:6]], AV (Waterland, Works, II, 108; Cremer, 649 f.; Meyer, in l; cf. also JThS, July, 1909, April, 1911; MM, see word). 
2. Passively = ἅρπαγμα ([[26-ezekiel.22.25|Eze.22:25]], of a lion's prey, ), **a thing seized, hence, a prize**: Phi, l.with, RV (Lft., Ellic., _ICC_, in l; Donaldson, NCrat., 450 ff.; and esp. Gifford, The Incarnation, 59-71, and reff. in _DB_, ii, 835 B). The lexical data favour the active meaning, but as they also admit the possibility of the alternative, most modern expositors have accepted the latter as seeming to suit the logic of the passage better. The lexical difficulty, however, remains (MM, see word, esp. the last ref.). As to the usage of St. Paul, he seems inclined to adopt the -μα form where it is appropriate (e.g. [[45-romans.11.9|Rom.11:9]], where cf. LXX; [[46-1-corinthians.13.9|1Co.13:9]], 2 Co 19), and there is certainly a presumption in favour of the active meaning here from the fact that he does not use the LXX ἅρπαγμα. Suggestions looking to a fresh exegesis are given in JThS, ll with
